import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Dataset provided as a string
data = """Person ID,Gender,Age,Occupation,Sleep Duration,Quality of Sleep,Physical Activity Level,Stress Level,BMI Category,Blood Pressure,Heart Rate,Daily Steps,Sleep Disorder
1,Male,27,Software Engineer,6.1,6,42,6,Overweight,126/83,77,4200,
2,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
3,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
4,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
5,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Set a professional and clean style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create a figure and a set of subplots
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between Sleep Duration and Quality of Sleep.
# We use 'BMI Category' for color to see if there are distinct patterns among different BMI groups.
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Sleep Duration',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='BMI Category',
    s=200,  # Set a fixed size for markers for better visibility with limited data points
    alpha=0.8,
    edgecolor='w', # Add white edge for better separation of markers
    linewidth=1
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Relationship between Sleep Duration and Quality of Sleep by BMI Category', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10 scale)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement to not overlap with the data points
plt.legend(title='BMI Category', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0, frameon=True)

# Add grid for easier reading of values
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Adjust plot layout to prevent labels from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300)
